newsitem.title: USA: Bank of New York processing revenue up 18 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bank of New York processing revenue up 18 pct.

text.p: Securities processing revenue at Bank of New York Co Inc rose to $190 million in the second quarter of 1997 from $161 million a year ago, a gain of 18 percent.

Bank of New York said in its earnings release Monday that strong internal growth in almost all areas drove the increase in revenue. The company said American Depositary Receipts (ADR's), corporate trust, government securities clearance, mutual funds and stock transfer were particularly strong.
Bank of New York said fees from other processing, including funds transfer, cash management, and trade finance rose 14 percent from the second quarter of 1996 with strong growth in all areas.
The company said trust and investment continued to benefit from new business and strong markets, with fees rising to $44 million in the second quarter from $40 million a year ago.

Net interest income, on a taxable equivalent basis, was $489 million in the second quarter, down from $502 million a year ago. The decrease reflected the sale of $4.3 billion of credit cards receivables.

Average full diluted shares fell to 399 million in the 1997 second quarter, down from 405 million in the first quarter of 1997 and 418 million a year ago. Bank of New York said the decline from the first quarter and prior year was the result of the company's stock buyback program.
